_comment: Hand-maintained boss preparation data: what to wear, carry and use to get to each boss. Planning before the trip only. Reasons for gear may mention a mechanic or prayer effect, as the wiki's strategy pages do, but never tell you what to do in the fight: no prayer instructions, timing, positioning or what's coming next. Boss keys are lower case. 'name' is shown in the picker. 'monsters' are the monsters to work out gear against, matched as 'Name (version)', or 'Name' for every version; the first is the default. 'wholeFight': true means every listed monster is fought on each trip (phases, or several monsters), so the plan wears the best set for the first and carries switches for the rest. 'slayerTask' marks bosses that can only be fought on that Slayer task. 'required' lists worn items, by slot, that the boss needs; any one name per slot satisfies it. 'prefer' lists worn items the wiki's strategy page recommends for reasons the DPS maths can't see: {'slot', 'items', 'withinPercent', 'reason'}; the gear search keeps one of the items when the best set without it is no more than withinPercent better. 'inventory' lists items to carry; each entry is satisfied by any one of its names (matched as a prefix, so 'Fungicide spray' matches 'Fungicide spray 10'); 'stackable': true means they fit in one slot, 'optional' means not flagged when missing, 'exact' means match names exactly. 'onlyFor' limits an item to one version of the boss, matched in its version (e.g. 'Awakened'). 'switch': true marks a swap the wiki recommends for part of the fight; it's carried only when owned and the Wiki switches setting is on, and its note says what it's for, never when to use it. 'dragonfire' is 'dragon' or 'wyvern'. 'venom': true marks bosses that poison or envenom you. 'stacks': true adds a Burst tab. 'comboEat': true brings karambwans. 'minWeight' is the least the worn gear must weigh, in kg. 'tips' are shown as they are. 'locations' are keys of 'locations', whose teleport 'items' are name prefixes used to tick off teleports you own (leave it out for spells or fairy rings). 'locationNeeds' are what a location itself needs: worn items ('required'), carried items ('inventory') and 'tips'.
